svg.text: Images, video, audio, vector, 3D and documents now mirrored with applications: the efficient modern format glows, the legacy one sinks. Lossless audio re-cut at full chroma — no green left in it.
blue images · green video · yellow-to-orange audio · purple documents · grey text & code · dark red apps · steel grey libraries
mirrored: rank 1 is the most efficient format and the BRIGHTEST rung; legacy formats sink into the dark end. Formats sharing a compressor share a rung (zip, jar and gz are all deflate)
lossless sits a few degrees round the wheel from lossy — indigo beside azure, full yellow beside full orange
the label colour is a property of the family, never of the file: no ramp ever crosses the white/dark ink boundary inside itself

svg.text: The band across the foot of each tile. The extension on the sheet is always the same dark ink — the sheet is white, so nothing switches there.
TreeMap view — where the ink rule actually bites

DrawTreeMapCell paints the caption in hard-coded white (UltraCanvasFilerWidget.cpp:9486). On the lightened audio and the grey text shades that is unreadable, so the caption ink has to come from the family.
dark on audio and text greys.
The three families left running the other way
Top row as proposed (rank 1 darkest); bottom row is the same ramp mirrored, if you want one global rule.

svg.text: Mirrored as asked: AVIF #2D86EA glows and GIF #0C3F7A sinks; WebM #1CA04B over WMV #0F5326; Opus #FFAA54 over MP3 #E27100; PDF #A876D4 over the markup formats at #5C2B87. Applications already ran this way.

Lossless audio re-cut at hue 48 and full chroma: #FFDC4D, #FDCA00, #EDBD00, #DEB200. The olive cast came from asking a saturated yellow to be dark — the ladder now stays above L 55 and the whole family reads as yellow.

Spreadsheets, Archives and Fonts still run the other way (rank 1 darkest) because they were not on your list. Spreadsheets sit in the purple band right beside Documents, so the two now rank in opposite directions — that is the one pairing where the inconsistency is visible.
The mirror does not change the ink rule: every family still clears 3.2:1 on a single ink, and the audio and text families keep dark captions.
